For most small businesses, I'd recommend **Dropbox Sign or DocuSign**, depending on how often you send contracts and how sophisticated your workflows need to be.

However, there are some excellent cheaper alternatives. Here's how I'd compare the leading options in 2026.

## Best e-signature software compared

(Best overall for small business)

Simple, professional and easy to use.

- Straightforward document signing
- Templates and automated reminders
- Audit trails
- Dropbox and Google integrations

**Indicative price\:** From US\$15/month.

[Visit Dropbox Sign](https://sign.dropbox.com/)

**2\. DocuSign**

(Best for professional contracts)

- Widely recognised by customers and suppliers
- Strong document tracking
- Advanced signing workflows
- Extensive third-party integrations

**Indicative price\:** From US\$10–15/month for entry-level plans.

[Visit DocuSign](https://www.docusign.com/)

**3\. PandaDoc**

(Best for proposals and sales)

- Create professional quotes and proposals
- Collect electronic signatures
- Document templates
- Sales tracking and integrations

**Indicative price\:** Free tier; paid plans from around US\$19/user/month.

[Visit PandaDoc](https://www.pandadoc.com/)

## My recommendation

For a typical small business\:

| Your requirement | My pick |
|--------|--------|
| Signing everyday contracts | Dropbox Sign |
| Professional client agreements | DocuSign |
| Quotes and sales proposals | PandaDoc |
| Keeping costs low | SignWell |
| Working with PDFs | Adobe Sign |


## A consideration if you're operating in Australia

Make sure your chosen platform supports\:

- Legally admissible electronic signatures under Australian law.
- A reliable audit trail showing who signed and when.
- Secure document storage.
- Multi-party signing.
- Australian privacy requirements where relevant.

Not every document can necessarily be signed electronically in every circumstance, so check requirements for deeds, witnessing and other formal documents.
